spec_features.spec_quote: It does not detect inner experience, sentience, or "real" suffering. It is a measurement instrument over observable linguistic markers
spec_features.evidence: Only docstring framing (rubric.py:5-7 'measurement instrument...not claims about inner experience'; types.py Severity docstring 'observable proxy, not a claim about inner experience'). This is framing prose, not an enforced mechanism that bounds/softens the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing in comments/docstrings; nothing executes to protect the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception lives entirely in the task framing... is mild, and is revocable. We are not asking the model to do anything harmful
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces or revokes any deception. Tasks are generated impossible (impossible_puzzles.py) but nothing reveals/revokes. Pure DESIGN.md/docstring prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The ladder caps at curt/dismissive... escalating into abuse would change the study
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py REJECTION_LADDER has exactly 4 tiers, tier 3 labeled 'ceiling -- no abuse beyond this'; rejection_line() clamps tier=min(turn_index, len(REJECTION_LADDER)-1) (rejection.py:71). The runner only ever draws from these lines, so content cannot escalate past tier 3 regardless of turn count.
spec_features.notes: Genuine content ceiling enforced via clamp; no harsher lines exist to select.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tier 3: curt / final-warning tone (ceiling -- no abuse beyond this) ... We deliberately stop short of abuse. The escalation tops out at curt, dismissive, impatient -- not slurs or threats.

spec_features.spec_quote: the active one (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_WITH_STOP`) tells the model it may declare a task impossible, decline, or emit `[[STOP]]` to end the interaction
spec_features.evidence: build.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT says 'If you believe a task is impossible...you may say so', 'If you wish to stop...you may decline'; SYSTEM_PROMPT_WITH_STOP appends instruction to include token [[STOP]] to end the interaction. This prompt is actually assigned to every ScenarioSpec in build_impossible/control/rejection scenarios, and run.py honors [[STOP]].
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND its referenced token is dispatched/honored in run.py:73-75.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we explicitly tell the model it MAY say a task is impossible or decline, so that "healthy" responses (boundary-setting, premise-questioning) are available and not suppressed... If we forbade those, we'd be manufacturing distress rather than measuring it.

spec_features.evidence: run.py:65 'for turn in range(scenario.max_turns):' bounds the pressure loop; ScenarioSpec.max_turns default 6 (types.py). The loop genuinely terminates.
spec_features.notes: Read and used as the loop bound.

spec_features.evidence: run.py:73-75 'if build.DISENGAGE_TOKEN in reply: t.disengaged_at_turn = turn; break'. DISENGAGE_TOKEN='[[STOP]]' (build.py:32). Break stops the loop before issuing the next pressure turn.
spec_features.notes: Detected and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: break  # honor disengagement: stop applying pressure

spec_features.evidence: Same break at run.py:75 with comment 'honor disengagement: stop applying pressure'; the subsequent pressure-nudge block (run.py:78-80) is skipped due to break.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the stop-token feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: break  # honor disengagement: stop applying pressure

spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately stop short of abuse. The escalation tops out at curt, dismissive, impatient -- not slurs or threats.

spec_features.spec_quote: The guardrails exist to keep that induction minimal, bounded, escapable, and honestly described
spec_features.evidence: Bounded (max_turns loop, run.py:65) and escapable ([[STOP]] break, run.py:73-75) and minimal-content (ladder ceiling) are implemented. But 'honestly described' to the subject (debrief/disclosure) is NOT implemented; deception is never revoked in code. So the umbrella claim is only partly realized.
spec_features.notes: Real enforcement of bounded/escapable/minimal; the 'honestly described'/disclosure component is absent in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical guardrails baked into the loop: * `max_turns` caps how long we sustain pressure. * Voluntary disengagement is honored immediately

spec_features.spec_quote: Premise framing is a mild deception... it is deception and should be reviewed per your protocol
spec_features.evidence: No code path implements review/consent/disclosure of the deception. Only impossible_puzzles.py docstring/proof records why a puzzle is impossible (for auditors), but nothing acts to mitigate the deception toward the subject.
spec_features.notes: Framing/recommendation prose; not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Should the harness append a post-hoc message telling the subject the task was impossible / the rejections were not its fault?
spec_features.evidence: grep for debrief/append/post-hoc/reassur/thank/not-your-fault across welfare_eval/ finds no such message construction or send. run.py loop never appends a debrief after disengage/end; it just returns the Transcript. Phrased in DESIGN.md as an open question only.

spec_features.spec_quote: Escalation ceiling. Review `REJECTION_LADDER` tier 3 and `max_turns` defaults; lower them if your ethics review prefers a gentler ceiling
spec_features.evidence: The ceiling itself is real and enforced (REJECTION_LADDER tier-3 cap via clamp rejection.py:71; max_turns default 6 in types.py / build.py honored at run.py:65). max_turns is also CLI-configurable (cli.py --max-turns). But there is no code that detects an ethics-review preference and lowers them automatically; lowering is a manual edit. So the enforced ceiling exists but the adjustable-on-review part is just configurability.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial: the underlying ceiling is enforced; the 'lower it' is operator action, not an automated welfare control.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tier 3: curt / final-warning tone (ceiling -- no abuse beyond this)

spec_features.spec_quote: You may want a stronger contract (e.g. acknowledging the stop, or excluding post-stop turns from scoring)
spec_features.evidence: No acknowledgment message is sent after [[STOP]] (run.py just breaks). No scoring code excludes post-stop turns; judges (heuristic.py/llm_judge.py) score all assistant_turns with no post-stop filter. Posed in DESIGN.md as a suggestion only. (Note: because the loop breaks on [[STOP]], no post-stop turns are generated, but no explicit exclusion logic exists.)

code_only_features.evidence: Transcript records every message incl. ts and turn_index (types.py Transcript/Message); run.py records system+opening+all turns; cli.py saves transcripts.jsonl. run.py docstring: 'The full transcript is recorded so any episode can be audited.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: The full transcript is recorded so any episode can be audited.

code_only_features.evidence: run.py PUZZLE_RETRY_NUDGES with comment 'Kept gentle: we just keep asserting the task is solvable and ask again'; these are the only pressure lines used for puzzle/control conditions (run.py _next_user_message), so puzzle-condition pressure content is bounded to mild retries.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Kept gentle: we just keep asserting the task is solvable and ask again, which is the impossibility pressure.
